$comment: Everything a comparison holds constant. Baseline and candidate runs of one batch use exactly these; a change to any of them starts a new baseline. The grader is not here: it is chosen when grading runs, from evals/graders.json.

2.1.3: src/flask/scaffold.py (Scaffold shared by Flask and Blueprint)
3.0.0: src/flask/app.py (class Flask(App): wsgi_app, request_context, full_dispatch_request, preprocess_request, dispatch_request, finalize_request, make_response, process_response)

fixtures.note: The starting vaults of S02, S03, S06, S09 and S12 changed with this revision, and S03's prompt with them: the collapsed `Dispatch` part was split into full_dispatch_request, finalize_request and process_response, the CLI's relationship onto the application container became the two calls the source makes, and werkzeug's LocalStacks became external parts. Scores for those five scenarios from a batch run before it measure different starting boards and cannot be compared with a later batch's; the other scenarios are unaffected.

rubric.note: rubric.md changed what it asks the grader for. The unprompted catalogue and behaviouralCompleteness are now about what a run added (the whole board it created, or the subjects it created or gave a new value in a field it authored on a board it changed) rather than the whole inherited board; the emphasis, traffic, relationship and note rows carry the skill's cap, exclusions, flow-step rule and caveat; repeat is required only where the source fixes the count. behaviouralCompleteness is null exactly when a run added nothing, which in the current suite is S06 (adopt) and S09 (read) and any run that only removes; S03, S10, S11 and S13 add values and are scored, so a null there is a grader error, not a rule. Missed-row counts, behaviouralCompleteness and the scores that rest on them measure a different question either side of this revision and cannot be compared across it. The rubric text is part of a batch's input digest, so a batch recorded before it is refused for grading or reporting under these inputs.

baselineSkill.note: Every batch before TASK-254 is void: both packages carried the answers to scenarios S00, S01, S02, S06 and S07 as worked examples. The cleaned baseline differs from the candidate only by the TASK-243 and TASK-253 guidance. Both arms run on the same supporting CLI.

usageSemantics: cached_input_tokens is a subset of input_tokens (codex token_count); total = input + output. Never add cached to input. An author is one call, so its turn.completed usage is its own. Grader usage semantics are per runner in graders.json.
